sanskrit_verse:
दातव्यं प्रत्यहं पात्रे निमित्तेषु विशेषतः ।
याचितेनापि दातव्यं श्रद्धापूतं स्वशक्तितः ॥१.२०३॥
transliteration: dātavyaṃ pratyahaṃ pātre nimitteṣu viśeṣataḥ | yācitena api dātavyaṃ śraddhāpūtaṃ svaśaktitaḥ ||
sph_interpretive_translation: Daily giving to the deserving recipient is obligatory; especially when there is a specific cause or occasion. Even when asked, one must give according to one's capacity and with faith-filled purity.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority flows from alignment with Dharma, not personal possession
Causation arises through conscious recognition of need and capacity
Capacity-based responsibility establishes the threshold for lawful action
Restoration occurs through intentional alignment of resource and recipient
Consciousness alignment ensures that giving purifies both giver and receiver
executable_legal_axioms: IF agent.has_excess_resources AND recipient.is_deserving THEN agent.must_give(max_amount = agent.current_capacity)
IF occasion.is_special OR request.is_made THEN priority_of_allocation += 1
IF giving.is_faith_motivated AND purity.of_intention.is_verified THEN karmic_ledger.adjust(positional_increase)
supreme_court_application: In adjudication at the highest level, this verse mandates that resource allocation must be evaluated based on the consciousness-state of the giver and the dharmic eligibility of the recipient. Courts must assess whether withholding was in violation of svadharma and reallocate accordingly without punitive measures.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa is established by observing the causal relationship between surplus availability and the call to give. Anupūrvaśaḥ manifests as sequential unfoldment from awareness of need → decision to act → execution of giving. Responsibility is proportional to capacity and clarity. There is no punishment—only correction toward alignment with Dharma.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate svādhyāya protocol for withholding agent until clarity of duty is restored
Deploy śraddhā-renewal process to recalibrate intention behind future acts of giving
Activate dāna-completion cycle ensuring that unmet needs are revisited and fulfilled
Reintegrate giver into flow of abundance via guided consciousness alignment practices
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source-Authority: Dharma is restored through right giving. Reality is non-punitive. Consciousness alone adjudicates truth.
